subject: Request: Precise sample logs & tokenization proof for June overage
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@logichain.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sawyer <tom.sawyer@logichain.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected token spike in early June — can you share precise logs?

Hi Marcus,

Hope you’re well. We noticed a sharp spike on June 10–12 that produced ~2.7x more billed tokens than our internal tracer. The invoice shows an overage charge for the mid-June period; we believe at least some of that delta is due to how tokens were sampled/attributed during a rolling-aggregation window on your side.

Can you provide: 1) a per-request sample of token counts and tokenization snapshots for a few representative requests (timestamps + request IDs), 2) any server-side changes to tokenization or sampling around June 9–13, and 3) the raw meter event rows for that account for the affected interval? We’ll map to our client-side logs.

We’ve placed the invoice on hold pending verification. Please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Integrations — LogiChain
---
attachment: logichain_usage_snapshot_20270610-20270617.csv (csv, 42KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@logichain.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token spike in early June — can you share precise logs?

Hi Emily — thanks for flagging this and for the snapshot. We dug into the logs and I wanted to share an initial set of artifacts while we run a deeper reconciliation:

- What I’m attaching: redwood_sample_logs_20270618.csv — this contains per-request meter events (request_id, server_timestamp, model_variant, raw_token_count, billed_token_count, aggregation_window_ms). We included three representative requests that map to the times you called out.
- Short explanation: On June 9 we rolled a minor batching change that tightened the aggregation window from 250ms to 200ms for a small subset of routes (aim: reduce tail latency). That change can shift how contiguous requests are coalesced into a single billed event, sometimes increasing the billed token count for a multi-turn payload.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll provide the full raw meter event dump for your account for Jun 9–13 (CSV S3 link below).
2) Naomi (cc’d, billing) can propose a one-time pro-rated credit if we confirm a clear attribution to our aggregation change.
3) If you prefer, we can walk the logs together in a short screen share.

S3 link (private): https://s3.redwood.company/logs/PLG-4892/20270609-20270613-meter.csv

We’ll follow up with the full export within 24 hours.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
---
attachment: redwood_sample_logs_20270618.csv (csv, 95KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@logichain.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token spike in early June — can you share precise logs?

Hi Emily,

Thank you for your patience while we validated the events. Naomi here from Billing. Summary of findings:

- Root cause: confirmed partial attribution to our 200ms aggregation window adjustment that increased coalescing for some concurrent multi-turn sessions. That change created a few merged meter events where billed_token_count exceeded the sum observed on LogiChain side because your client traces were recorded per-turn before server coalescing.
- Impact: six aggregated events in the interval Jun 10–12 accounted for ~18% of the reported overage (we show the full event rows in the attached CSV).
- Proposal: Redwood is prepared to issue a one-time goodwill credit that covers the verified delta for those aggregated events. Attached is a proposed credit table (proposed-credit-table-PLG-4892.xlsx) with line items and calculation. Total proposed credit: $3,175.

A few administrative notes:
1) To apply the credit to the outstanding invoice we need a short confirmation reply from LogiChain authorizing the adjustment and whether you want the credit applied against the current invoice or as a bill credit against future invoices.
2) If LogiChain prefers to hold the invoice until reconciliation is complete, we’ll flag finance to delay collections for up to 30 days while we finalize export reconciliation (we’ll need a PO or short ‘invoice hold’ confirmation email).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the rows if helpful.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Billing Manager — Redwood Inference
---

Subject: Re: Unexpected token spike in early June — can you share precise logs?

Hi Naomi / Marcus,

Thanks for the quick investigation and for the proposed credit. We’ve reviewed the sample rows and the calculation looks sensible. LogiChain confirms authorization to apply the $3,175 credit to the current outstanding invoice. Please proceed and send an updated invoice when the credit has been applied.

We’ll also schedule a short follow-up next week to review routing and batching options to avoid similar coalescing effects.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Integrations — LogiChain
